examples.ko: 우리는 산 능선을 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: We walked slowly along the mountain ridge.

examples.ko: 능선 위에서 보는 해돋이가 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: The sunrise seen from the ridge is really beautiful.
When the fog cleared, a distant ridge came into view.

examples.ko: 바람이 센 능선에서는 모자를 꼭 잡아야 해요.
examples.en: On a windy ridge, you have to hold your hat tight.

examples.ko: 저 능선만 넘으면 마을이 나올 거예요.
examples.en: Once we cross that ridge, we'll reach the village.

examples.ko: 이 능선은 길이 좁아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The path on this ridge is narrow, so be careful.

explain: 산에서 '산꼭대기'는 제일 높은 한 점이고, '능선'은 그 꼭대기들을 이어 주는 길쭉한 선이에요. 등산 이야기에서 '능선을 타다', '능선을 따라 걷다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '산꼭대기' is the single highest point, while 능선 is the long line that connects the peaks. In hiking talk you often hear '능선을 타다' or '능선을 따라 걷다'.

examples.en: The Korean delegation arrived this morning.

examples.ko: 대표단은 회의가 끝난 뒤 기자들과 만났어요.
examples.en: After the meeting, the delegation met with reporters.

examples.ko: 우리 학교도 대표단을 뽑아서 보내기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our school also decided to choose and send a delegation.

examples.ko: 대표단 열 명이 같은 비행기를 탔어요.
examples.en: Ten members of the delegation took the same plane.
The company toured the site together with the delegation.
We sent our support to the delegation going to the Olympics.

explain: '대표'는 한 사람일 수도 있지만 '대표단'은 여러 사람이 한 팀으로 가는 경우에 써요. 나라, 학교, 회사처럼 큰 곳이 다른 곳에 사람들을 보낼 때 자주 들어요.
explain_en: 대표 can be one person, but 대표단 means a team of several people sent together. You hear it when a country, school, or company sends a group elsewhere.

examples.en: People ran away, startled by the boar's charge.
That team's charge was really scary.
I couldn't avoid the car's sudden rush forward.

examples.ko: 선수들이 골대를 향해 돌진 준비를 했어요.
examples.en: The players got ready to charge toward the goal.
After endless charging ahead, I finally succeeded.

examples.ko: 돌진이 너무 빨라서 막을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The rush was so fast that we couldn't stop it.

explain: '돌진'은 앞에 뭐가 있어도 멈추지 않고 세게 달려드는 움직임이에요. '달리기'가 그냥 빨리 가는 것이라면 '돌진'은 힘으로 밀고 들어가는 느낌이에요. 사람보다 동물이나 차, 스포츠 이야기에 잘 나오고, '돌진하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: 돌진 is a movement that keeps pushing forward hard no matter what is ahead. Where 달리기 is just running fast, 돌진 feels like driving in by force. It shows up more with animals, cars, and sports, and the verb form is 돌진하다.

examples.en: The cow suddenly charged toward us.

examples.ko: 버스가 가게 앞으로 돌진해서 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The bus rushed toward the shop, and it almost became a disaster.
The player charges forward with the ball.
He is someone who charges toward his goals.
My friends rushed inside as soon as the door opened.

examples.ko: 멈추지 않고 돌진하면 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you charge without stopping, you can get hurt.

explain: '달리다'는 그냥 빠르게 움직이는 것이고, '돌진하다'는 앞에 뭐가 있어도 멈추지 않고 세게 들어가는 거예요. 동물, 차, 운동선수가 주어일 때가 많고, 사람의 의욕을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: 달리다 just means moving fast, while 돌진하다 means pushing forward hard without stopping for whatever is ahead. The subject is often an animal, vehicle, or athlete, and it can also describe a person's drive.

examples.en: The soup is boiling on the stove.
Please turn down the stove heat.
I bought a new stove, and the kitchen looks clean.
The stove in my house runs on electricity.

examples.ko: 레인지가 고장 나서 수리 기사님을 불렀어요.
examples.en: The stove broke, so I called a repairman.

examples.ko: 요리하기 전에 레인지 주변을 먼저 닦았어요.
examples.en: I wiped around the stove before cooking.

explain: '레인지'는 '가스레인지'나 '전기레인지'(불이나 열로 요리하는 조리대)를 줄인 말이기도 하고, '전자레인지'를 줄인 말이기도 해요. 그래서 '레인지에 돌리다'는 보통 전자레인지를 뜻해요. 조리대를 말할 때는 헷갈리지 않게 '가스레인지', '전기레인지'처럼 앞말을 붙이는 편이 안전해요.
explain_en: 레인지 is a short form of both 가스레인지/전기레인지 (a cooktop) and 전자레인지 (a microwave), so '레인지에 돌리다' usually means heating food in the microwave. To refer to a cooktop without confusion, it is safer to add a word first, as in 가스레인지 or 전기레인지.

examples.en: That judge is famous for fair rulings.
To become a judge, you have to study for a long time.
The courtroom went quiet at the judge's single remark.
Young judges have started their new jobs.
My older sister has dreamed of being a judge since childhood.
What a judge needs is fairness.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '판사'를 더 많이 쓰고, '법관'은 뉴스나 글에서 판사를 넓게 가리킬 때 나와요. 그래서 '법관'은 조금 딱딱한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say 판사 more often. 법관 appears in news and writing as a broader, more formal word for judges, so it sounds stiff.

examples.en: I bought a bikini for my summer vacation.

examples.ko: 그녀는 파란 비키니를 입고 바다로 갔어요.
examples.en: She went to the sea wearing a blue bikini.
I wore a thin shirt over my bikini.
I put the bikini in my bag.
This shop sells bikinis too.
The bikini got too small, so I have to buy a new one.

explain: 수영복은 '수영복'이 가장 일반적이고, '비키니'는 위아래가 나뉜 수영복만 가리켜요. 한 벌로 된 수영복은 보통 '원피스 수영복'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 수영복 is the general word for swimwear, while 비키니 means only the two-piece kind. A one-piece suit is usually called '원피스 수영복'.

examples.en: The two of them pledged to stay together for life.

examples.ko: 신입 사원들이 서약을 하고 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The new employees took a pledge and began work.
I wrote my name on the pledge form and stamped it.

examples.ko: 학생들은 정직하게 시험을 보겠다는 서약을 했어요.
examples.en: The students made a pledge to take the exam honestly.
That pledge was not broken easily.
At the wedding, the bride and groom read their vows.

explain: '약속'은 일상에서 가볍게 쓰지만 '서약'은 맹세처럼 무겁고 공식적인 약속이에요. 보통 '서약을 하다'라고 하고, 문서로 쓰면 '서약서'라고 불러요.
explain_en: 약속 is a light, everyday promise, but 서약 is a heavy, formal promise close to an oath. You usually say '서약을 하다', and the written form is called 서약서.

en: seonnyeo; heavenly maiden; celestial nymph in folk tales

examples.en: In old tales there is a heavenly maiden who comes down from the sky.
The heavenly maiden lived with the woodcutter.
She wore beautiful clothes like a heavenly maiden.
The kids listened to the story of the heavenly maiden and the woodcutter.
The heavenly maiden in her feather robe rose to the sky.
In the play, I took the role of the heavenly maiden.

explain: '선녀'는 한국 옛이야기 '선녀와 나무꾼'에 나오는 하늘의 여자예요. 서양의 '요정'과 비슷해 보이지만 날개옷을 입고 하늘에서 내려온다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: 선녀 is the heavenly woman in the Korean folk tale '선녀와 나무꾼'. She resembles a Western fairy (요정), but she comes from heaven wearing a feather robe.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 올해 승률이 아주 높아요.
examples.en: This team has a very high win rate this year.
As the win rate went up, fans increased.
Our team's win rate is sixty percent.
I practice every day to raise my win rate.

examples.ko: 지난 시즌 승률보다 올해가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: This year is better than last season's win rate.
The coach did not obsess only over the win rate.

explain: '승률'은 이긴 횟수를 전체 경기 수로 나눈 비율이에요. 야구, 축구, 게임 이야기에서 '승률이 높다/낮다'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: 승률 is the share of games won out of all games played. It comes up in baseball, soccer, and gaming as '승률이 높다/낮다'.

examples.en: The two of them got engaged last month.
We decided to get engaged next spring.
My friend said she is getting engaged to her longtime partner.
Engaged couples introduce each other to their families.

examples.ko: 그는 약혼해서 요즘 아주 행복해 보여요.
examples.en: He got engaged, so he looks very happy these days.
When people get engaged, they often exchange rings.

explain: '약혼하다'는 결혼하기로 약속하는 것이고 '결혼하다'는 실제로 부부가 되는 거예요. 약혼한 사람은 '약혼자'라고 불러요. 결혼 약속 전에 양가 부모님이 만나는 자리는 '상견례'라고 해요.
explain_en: 약혼하다 means promising to marry, while 결혼하다 means actually becoming a married couple. A person you are engaged to is a 약혼자. The meeting where both sets of parents get together is called 상견례.

examples.en: My younger brother has had asthma since childhood.

examples.ko: 천식 때문에 먼지가 많은 곳은 피해요.
examples.en: Because of asthma, I avoid dusty places.

examples.ko: 갑자기 찬 바람을 맞으면 천식이 심해져요.
examples.en: Asthma gets worse if I suddenly face cold wind.
The doctor prescribed asthma medicine.
It is important to manage asthma consistently.

examples.ko: 아이가 밤에 천식으로 기침을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: The child coughed a lot at night because of asthma.

explain: '감기'는 며칠 지나면 낫지만 '천식'은 오래 가는 병이에요. '천식이 있어요'라고 하면 평소에 가진 병이라는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: 감기 goes away in a few days, but 천식 is a long-lasting condition. Saying '천식이 있어요' implies it is a condition you live with.

examples.en: The communication network went down because of the typhoon.
A new network was installed, and the internet got faster.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 통신망이 약해서 전화가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: The network is weak in this area, so calls often fail.
The company overhauled its communication network.

examples.ko: 통신망 공사 때문에 오전에 연결이 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The connection failed in the morning due to network work.
It is hard to connect to the network in the mountains.

explain: '네트워크'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 '통신망'은 전화나 인터넷처럼 연결된 통신 설비를 말해서 조금 더 공식적이에요. '통신망이 끊기다', '통신망이 복구되다'처럼 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is close to 네트워크, but 통신망 refers to the connected telecom infrastructure such as phone and internet lines, and sounds a bit more official. In the news you hear '통신망이 끊기다' and '통신망이 복구되다'.

examples.en: Please check the documents carefully.
He handles everything thoroughly.
I read the exam paper again carefully.
Look through the contract carefully and sign it.
When cleaning, I wiped even the corners carefully.

examples.ko: 메모를 꼼꼼히 남겨 두면 나중에 편해요.
examples.en: If you keep careful notes, it is easier later.

explain: '꼼꼼'은 '꼼꼼하다'의 어근이라 실제 대화에서는 '꼼꼼히', '꼼꼼하게', '꼼꼼한 사람'처럼 모양을 바꿔 써요. 반대로 대충 하는 것은 '대충'이나 '건성으로'라고 해요.
explain_en: 꼼꼼 is the root of 꼼꼼하다, so in real speech it appears as 꼼꼼히, 꼼꼼하게, or 꼼꼼한 사람. The opposite, doing something sloppily, is 대충 or '건성으로'.

examples.en: The shop was designed with customers' movement paths in mind.

examples.ko: 이 부엌은 동선이 짧아서 요리하기 편해요.
examples.en: This kitchen has a short path, so it is easy to cook in.

examples.ko: 여행 동선을 미리 짜 두면 시간을 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you plan your travel route in advance, you can save time.
The movements of the infected person were released in the news.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 동선이 겹쳐서 자주 마주쳤어요.
examples.en: Their paths overlapped, so they often ran into each other.

examples.ko: 동선이 꼬이면 오히려 더 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: If the route gets tangled, it actually takes longer.

explain: '길'은 땅 위의 길이고 '동선'은 사람이 움직이는 흐름이나 순서예요. 집, 가게, 여행 계획을 세울 때 '동선을 짜다', '동선이 편하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 길 is a physical road, while 동선 is the flow or order in which a person moves. When planning a home, shop, or trip you say '동선을 짜다' or '동선이 편하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 문화원에서 한국어 수업을 들어요.
examples.en: Every weekend I take a Korean class at the cultural center.
There is a Korean cultural center in this city.
The cultural center held a hanbok experience event.
I decided to meet a friend in front of the cultural center.
The cultural center is closed on Mondays.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 문화원에서 무료 전시를 해요.
examples.en: The cultural center in my neighborhood has a free exhibition.

explain: '문화원'은 한 나라의 문화를 소개하고 강좌나 전시를 여는 기관이에요. 외국에 있는 '한국문화원', 한국 안의 '지역 문화원'처럼 앞에 이름을 붙여서 말해요.
explain_en: 문화원 is an institution that introduces a country's culture through classes and exhibitions. People attach a name in front, as in '한국문화원' abroad or a local 문화원 within Korea.

examples.en: I set down a step stool to reach the high shelf.

examples.ko: 현관 앞 발판에 신발의 흙을 털었어요.
examples.en: I shook the dirt off my shoes on the mat at the front door.
This footboard is slippery, so it is dangerous.

examples.ko: 버스에 오를 때 발판이 높아서 조심했어요.
examples.en: The step was high when I boarded the bus, so I was careful.

examples.ko: 그는 이번 성공을 발판 삼아 더 크게 도전했어요.
examples.en: He took on a bigger challenge using this success as a stepping stone.
I put my foot on the bicycle pedal.

explain: 발이 닿는 판이라는 뜻에서 계단, 받침, 문 앞 매트까지 넓게 써요. 비유로는 '발판이 되다', '발판으로 삼다'처럼 다음 단계로 가는 기반이라는 뜻이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이번 경험을 발판으로 삼아 더 높은 목표에 도전할래요.
phrases.en: to use as a stepping stone
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 발판이 아니라 다음 성공을 위한 바탕으로 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean a real platform but using something as a base for the next success.

explain_en: The word covers anything your foot rests on, from a step or footrest to a doormat. Figuratively, '발판이 되다' and '발판으로 삼다' mean a base for reaching the next stage.

examples.en: He disguised himself to avoid the police.
The kids dressed up as witches at the party.
Even if you disguise yourself, I know you from your voice.
The scene where the actor disguises himself as a grandmother was funny.
They say a celebrity came to the market in disguise.
She was disguised, so nobody recognized her.

explain: '변장하다'는 정체를 숨기거나 다른 사람처럼 보이려고 옷차림과 얼굴을 바꾸는 거예요. 배우가 역할에 맞게 꾸미는 건 '분장'이라고 해요. '변장'은 누군가를 속이거나 알아보지 못하게 하려는 목적이 있을 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 변장하다 means changing your clothes and face to hide who you are or pass as someone else. When an actor is made up for a role, the word is 분장. 변장 fits best when the aim is to fool people or avoid being recognized.

examples.en: The police put handcuffs on the criminal.
A man in handcuffs went into the court.
In the movie, the hero slipped out of the handcuffs and escaped.
The handcuffs were too tight on the wrist.
A suspect in handcuffs appeared on the news.

examples.ko: 그는 수갑 때문에 손목에 자국이 생겼어요.
examples.en: He got marks on his wrists from the handcuffs.

explain: 수갑은 '채우다', '차다', '풀다'와 함께 써요. 누가 채우면 '수갑을 채우다', 내가 차면 '수갑을 차다'라고 해서 동사가 달라져요.
explain_en: 수갑 goes with 채우다, 차다, and 풀다. When someone puts them on another person it is '수갑을 채우다', and for the wearer it is '수갑을 차다', so the verb changes.

examples.en: Lotus flowers have bloomed fully in the pond.
I want to go to the lotus festival in summer.

examples.ko: 연꽃은 진흙 속에서 자라지만 깨끗해 보여요.
examples.en: A lotus grows in mud but looks clean.

examples.ko: 절 마당에 연꽃 등이 걸려 있었어요.
examples.en: Lotus lanterns were hanging in the temple yard.

examples.ko: 그림 속 연꽃이 아주 곱게 그려졌어요.
examples.en: The lotus flower in the painting is drawn very delicately.
My friend sent me a photo of lotus flowers.

explain: '연꽃'은 불교와 관련이 깊어서 절에서 자주 보이는 꽃이에요. 식물은 '연', 잎은 '연잎'이라고 해서 음식 '연잎밥'에도 이 말이 들어가요.
explain_en: 연꽃 is closely tied to Buddhism and is often seen at temples. The plant is 연 and its leaf is 연잎, which is also why the dish 연잎밥 has this word in it.

examples.ko: 그는 연예계에서 활동한 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: He has been active in the entertainment industry for ten years.
News of the entertainment world spreads fast.
My younger sister dreams of working in the entertainment industry.
The entertainment industry is extremely competitive.
An actor who left the entertainment industry returned after a long time.
People in showbiz get attention on their private lives too.

explain: '연예인'은 배우, 가수, 방송인 같은 사람이고 '연예계'는 그 사람들이 활동하는 업계 전체예요. '연예계에 데뷔하다', '연예계를 떠나다', '연예계 소식'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 연예인 is a person such as an actor, singer, or TV personality, while 연예계 is the whole industry where they work. It is used as in '연예계에 데뷔하다', '연예계를 떠나다', and '연예계 소식'.

examples.en: I saw a large oil painting at the art museum.
She paints oil paintings every weekend.

examples.ko: 유화는 마르는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Oil paintings take a long time to dry.

examples.ko: 아버지가 거실에 유화 한 점을 걸었어요.
examples.en: My father hung an oil painting in the living room.
The smell of oil paint spread through the room.
Oil painting is harder for me than watercolor.

explain: 그림 종류는 '유화'와 '수채화'를 같이 외우면 좋아요. 유화는 기름 물감으로 두껍게 그리는 그림이고, 수채화는 물을 섞어 연하게 그려요.
explain_en: It helps to learn 유화 together with 수채화. 유화 is thick painting in oil paint, while 수채화 is light painting mixed with water.

examples.en: I made fried eggs for breakfast.
Please put one more fried egg on top.
I put sausage and a fried egg in the lunch box.
A fried egg gets hard if you cook it too long.

examples.ko: 저는 노른자가 반쯤 익은 프라이를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like fried eggs with half-cooked yolks.

examples.ko: 밥 위에 프라이를 올리니까 더 맛있어졌어요.
examples.en: Putting a fried egg on the rice made it tastier.

explain: 한국에서 '프라이'는 대부분 '계란 프라이'를 줄인 말로 써요. 영어 fry보다 훨씬 좁은 뜻이라서, 감자튀김은 '프라이'가 아니라 '감자튀김'이나 '프렌치프라이'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea 프라이 mostly means 계란 프라이 in short, a much narrower sense than English fry. French fries are called 감자튀김 or 프렌치프라이, not just 프라이.

examples.ko: 저는 비행기 공포증이 있어서 해외여행을 못 가요.
examples.en: I have a fear of flying, so I can't travel abroad.

examples.ko: 동생은 개 공포증이 있어서 산책을 싫어해요.
examples.en: My younger brother has a fear of dogs, so he dislikes walks.

examples.ko: 그는 공포증을 이기려고 상담을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is getting counseling to overcome his phobia.
My hands shake because of my fear of presenting.

examples.ko: 공포증은 노력하면 조금씩 나아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: A phobia can improve little by little with effort.
Many people have a fear of elevators.

explain: '무섭다'는 그때그때의 느낌이고, '공포증'은 특정한 것을 지나치게 무서워하는 상태예요. '고소공포증', '폐쇄공포증'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 한 단어로 써요.
explain_en: 무섭다 is a feeling in the moment, while 공포증 is a condition of excessive fear of a specific thing. The target is attached in front as one word, like 고소공포증 or 폐쇄공포증.

examples.en: The staff parking lot is behind the school.
The faculty and staff prepared an event for the students.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 교직원만 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only school staff can use this restaurant.
The staff meeting is every Monday.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 교직원 열 명이 새로 왔어요.
examples.en: Ten new staff members arrived for the new semester.
If you ask the staff, they will tell you in detail.

explain: '교사'는 가르치는 사람이고 '교직원'은 교사와 행정 직원까지 학교에서 일하는 사람 전체예요. 대학에서는 '교수'와 '직원'을 합쳐서 '교직원'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: 교사 means a teacher, while 교직원 covers everyone working at a school, including teachers and administrative staff. At a university it combines 교수 and 직원.

examples.ko: 곰팡이 핀 음식에는 독소가 있을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Moldy food can contain toxins.

examples.ko: 몸의 독소를 빼 주는 음료가 인기예요.
examples.en: Drinks that remove toxins from the body are popular.

examples.ko: 이 버섯은 독소가 강해서 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This mushroom has strong toxins, so you must not eat it.

examples.ko: 간은 몸속 독소를 걸러 주는 역할을 해요.
examples.en: The liver filters toxins in the body.

examples.ko: 복어의 독소는 열을 가해도 없어지지 않아요.
examples.en: Pufferfish toxin does not disappear even with heat.

examples.ko: 독소 때문에 식중독에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get food poisoning because of toxins.

explain: '독'은 해로운 물질 전체를 가리키는 말이고, '독소'는 생물이나 몸 안에서 만들어지거나 쌓이는 해로운 물질에 주로 써요. 요즘은 건강 광고에서 '독소 배출'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 독 is the general word for any harmful substance, while 독소 mostly refers to harmful substances made or built up in living things or the body. Health ads these days often use '독소 배출'.

examples.en: It rains in the southeast region from the afternoon.
A lot of sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The wind is blowing from the southeast.
My house faces southeast, so it is warm.

examples.ko: 동남 방향으로 십 분만 걸으면 역이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk ten minutes southeast, you reach the station.
I traveled to Southeast Asia.

explain: '남동'도 같은 방향이에요. '동남아', '동남향', '동남권'처럼 굳은 말에는 '동남'을 써요. 지도나 날씨 이야기에는 두 말이 다 나와요.
explain_en: 남동 means the same direction. Set terms like 동남아, 동남향, and 동남권 use 동남. On maps and in weather talk, both forms appear.

examples.en: It is dangerous if people go onto the tracks.

examples.ko: 선로 공사 때문에 기차가 늦게 와요.
examples.en: The train comes late because of track work.
A cat was walking along the tracks.

examples.ko: 지하철 선로에 물건을 떨어뜨리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not drop things onto the subway tracks.
The tracks were flooded by the heavy rain.
A staff member is inspecting the tracks.

explain: '선로'는 기차나 지하철이 다니는 철로 전체를 말해요. 뉴스와 안내방송에서 '선로 점검', '선로 안전'처럼 자주 들리고, 일상에서는 '철길'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: 선로 means the railway tracks that trains and subways run on. You hear it in the news and announcements as '선로 점검' or '선로 안전', and in daily speech people also say 철길.

examples.ko: 농장에서는 큰 귤을 선별해서 따로 담아요.
examples.en: The farm sorts out large tangerines and packs them separately.

examples.ko: 이 일은 선별 작업이 가장 힘들어요.
examples.en: The sorting work is the hardest part of this job.
I went through a screening check at the airport.
Without criteria, selection is hard.
The selection process was fair, so there were no complaints.

examples.ko: 여러 사진 중에서 선별을 하는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to select from among many photos.

explain: '선별'은 많은 것 중에서 기준에 맞는 것만 골라내는 거예요. '선택'은 하나를 고르는 느낌이고, '선별'은 여러 개를 가려내는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 선별 is picking out only the items that meet a standard from a large pool. 선택 feels like choosing one, while 선별 feels like screening out several.

examples.ko: 좋은 사과만 선별해서 선물 상자에 담았어요.
examples.en: I selected only good apples and put them in the gift box.
Please select a few photos.
The interviewer carefully screens applicants.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 믿을 만한 정보만 선별하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to pick only reliable information from the news.
We brought in a new machine to sort out defective items.
After selecting which books to keep, the luggage was halved.

explain: '고르다'는 마음에 드는 것을 고르는 일상적인 말이고, '선별하다'는 기준을 갖고 필요한 것만 가려내는 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.
explain_en: 고르다 is the everyday word for choosing what you like, while 선별하다 is a stiffer word for filtering out only what you need by a standard.

examples.en: My younger brother is well-behaved in front of strangers.
Our cat was calm at the vet.
The child sits quietly and reads a book.

examples.ko: 얌전한 줄 알았는데 말하면 재미있는 사람이에요.
examples.en: I thought he was quiet, but he is fun once he talks.
You should behave yourself during class.
That puppy is well-behaved, so it is easy to raise.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 없다는 뜻이고 '얌전하다'는 행동이 차분하고 말썽을 안 부리는 거예요. 아이나 동물에게 칭찬으로 많이 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 조금 답답한 느낌이 날 때도 있어요.
explain_en: 조용하다 is about lack of noise, while 얌전하다 is about calm behavior without making trouble. It is a common compliment for kids and animals, though for adults it can sometimes sound a bit stuffy.

examples.en: Infants sleep about fifteen hours a day.

examples.ko: 이 약은 영아에게 먹이면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not give this medicine to infants.
I need to buy a chair made for infants.
We got the infant vaccinations at the hospital.

examples.ko: 영아가 울면 먼저 기저귀를 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: If an infant cries, first check the diaper.

examples.ko: 이 놀이방은 영아와 부모가 같이 올 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this playroom, infants and parents can come together.

explain: '아기'는 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '영아'는 아주 어린 아기를 가리키는 의학, 행정 용어예요. 정확한 나이 범위는 법과 제도에 따라 달라요. 안내문과 뉴스에서 '영아'를 자주 만나요.
explain_en: 아기 is the everyday word, while 영아 is a medical and administrative term for a very young baby. The exact age range depends on the law or system. You meet it on notices and in the news.

examples.ko: 두 친구는 십 년 만에 재회했어요.
examples.en: The two friends reunited after ten years.

examples.ko: 공항에서 가족과 재회하는 순간 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I reunited with my family at the airport, I cried.
We promised to meet again in our hometown.
We reunited after a long time and talked all night.
They say the couple who had broken up met again by chance.

examples.ko: 언젠가 그 친구와 꼭 재회하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to be reunited with that friend someday.

explain: '만나다'는 어떤 만남이든 쓰지만 '재회하다'는 오래 헤어졌던 사람과 다시 만나는 순간에 써요. 드라마 줄거리에 자주 나오고, 평소 대화에서는 '다시 만나다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 만나다 works for any meeting, but 재회하다 is for meeting again someone you were apart from for a long time, usually with emotion. It appears often in drama plots, while '다시 만나다' is more natural in casual talk.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 전교에서 일 등을 했어요.
examples.en: That student came first in the whole school.
All students in the school gathered on the field.

examples.ko: 전교 회장 선거가 다음 주에 있어요.
examples.en: The school-wide president election is next week.

examples.ko: 전교생이 오백 명쯤 되는 작은 학교예요.
examples.en: It is a small school with about five hundred students.
An announcement came over the school-wide broadcast.
This news spread quickly through the whole school.

explain: '전교'는 '학교 전체'라는 뜻으로 '전교 1등', '전교 회장', '전교생'처럼 굳어진 말이 많아요. '전교 전체'처럼 겹쳐 쓰지는 않아요.
explain_en: 전교 means the whole school and is used in fixed phrases like 전교 1등, 전교 회장, and 전교생. People do not repeat it as '전교 전체'.

examples.en: I went to watch at the drama set.
The filming location was crowded with people from morning.
The actor was reading the script at the set.

examples.ko: 촬영장 근처에서 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos near the set.
Our village was used as a movie location.
I met the director as soon as I arrived at the set.

explain: '촬영장'은 영화나 드라마를 찍는 곳이고, '촬영지'는 실제로 찍은 장소예요. 팬들은 드라마의 '촬영지'를 일부러 찾아가기도 해요.
explain_en: 촬영장 is the place where a film or drama is shot, while 촬영지 is the actual real-world place where scenes were filmed. Fans sometimes travel to a drama's 촬영지 on purpose.

en: take a leave of absence from school

examples.ko: 저는 일 년 동안 휴학하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to take a year off from school.
My friend took a leave of absence because of poor health.
I plan to take a leave and go traveling.
Many students take leave to go to the military.
I took a leave and saved money with a part-time job.
If you take a leave, you don't have to pay tuition?

explain: '쉬다'와 달리 '휴학하다'는 학교에 정식으로 신청해서 학생 신분을 유지한 채 잠시 쉬는 거예요. 학교를 아예 그만두는 '자퇴하다', 학교로 돌아가는 '복학하다'와 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Unlike 쉬다, 휴학하다 means formally applying to the school to pause while keeping student status. Learn it with 자퇴하다, quitting school entirely, and 복학하다, returning to school.

en: open a business; set up a practice

examples.en: My uncle opens a restaurant next month.
The doctor opened a clinic in the neighborhood.
It has been a year since we opened.
That bakery became popular as soon as it opened.

examples.ko: 개업하기 전에 준비할 게 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot to prepare before opening a business.
I want to open a cafe someday.

explain: '개업하다'는 가게나 사무실을 처음 열고 영업을 시작하는 거예요. 매일 아침 문을 여는 건 '문을 열다'라고 해요. 영업을 완전히 그만두는 건 '폐업하다'예요.
explain_en: 개업하다 is opening a shop or office and starting business for the first time. Opening the door each morning is '문을 열다'. Closing a business for good is 폐업하다.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 오랜 연애 끝에 결별했어요.
examples.en: The two broke up after a long relationship.
An article said the singer is parting ways with the agency.
He decided to break with his old habits.
The two countries cut ties with their long alliance.
I was very hurt after parting from my friend.
Parting from the company was not easy.

explain: '헤어지다'는 연인이나 친구에게 두루 쓰는 말이고, '결별하다'는 관계를 끊는다는 의미가 강한 딱딱한 말이에요. 연예 기사에서 '결별설'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 헤어지다 is the all-purpose word for couples and friends, while 결별하다 is a stiff word stressing the cutting of ties. It often appears in entertainment articles as '결별설'.

examples.en: Grandmother looked out the window with a worried face.
The child's fever won't go down, so I am anxious.
He answered the phone in an anxious voice.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 근심스러워서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I was worried about the exam result and couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 표정이 근심스러워 보이는데 무슨 일 있어요?
examples.en: You look worried, is something wrong?

examples.ko: 부모님은 늘 제 건강을 근심스럽게 보세요.
examples.en: My parents always look at my health with concern.

explain: '걱정되다'는 일상에서 흔하고 '근심스럽다'는 걱정이 얼굴이나 분위기에 드러난다는 느낌의 글말에 가까워요. 보통 '근심스러운 얼굴', '근심스러운 표정'처럼 모습을 꾸며 줘요.
explain_en: 걱정되다 is the everyday choice, while 근심스럽다 is more bookish and implies the worry shows in a face or atmosphere. It usually modifies appearance, as in '근심스러운 얼굴' or '근심스러운 표정'.

examples.ko: 보물 상자 안에 금화가 가득 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: The treasure chest was full of gold coins.
In the old days people paid with gold coins.
They say the pirates hid gold coins.

examples.ko: 게임에서 금화를 모으면 아이템을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: In the game, you can buy items if you collect gold coins.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 천 년 된 금화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a thousand-year-old gold coin at the museum.

examples.ko: 금화 한 닢이 얼마나 되는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how much one gold coin is worth.

explain: '금화'는 금으로 만든 동전이에요. 은으로 만든 건 '은화', 지금 쓰는 동전은 '동전'이라고 해요. 옛이야기나 게임에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: 금화 is a coin made of gold. A silver one is 은화, and the coins used today are just 동전. It shows up often in old tales and games.
